out_of_scope: src/engine/eng_list.rs:90 (P25-ENGINE-CB-000, engine_list_cleanup): retained BLOCKED — lifetime/ordering of the unlocked Acquire load and the list-removal reference transition is unproven; distinct callback.
src/engine/eng_dyn.rs:401 (dynamic_data_ctx_free_func): retained BLOCKED — CRYPTO_EX_free hook with caller-supplied pointer; distinct ownership interior.
all other C_ABI_CONTRACT sites (look_str_cb, ui/conf callbacks, async shims): not enumerated here; the mechanism is NOT mechanism-wide discharged.
scope.statement: This is a scoped mechanism package for nine mechanically identical cleanup thunks, not a discharge of C_ABI_CONTRACT as a whole.

source_identity.head_subject: feat(analyzer): qualify the context object for static-table dispatch

environment.venue: docker/openssl-rs-court.sh (minimal court container; host checkout at /work)
environment.tsan: NOT_RUN (B20 ran TSan on eng_table previously; not re-run here)

chosen.criterion_applied: Every unsafe operation is one enumerated call to `engine_table_cleanup(<module-static slot>)`; the caller set is a single internal cleanup-stack walk with no caller-supplied pointer; the nine are one mechanically identical class and the pattern is reusable for engine static-table cleanup.
chosen.why_not_count: The 9 are chosen for enumerability and caller-contract establishability, not because they are few. Their caller contract is the smallest in the closure that is still a real, reusable ABI edge.

rejected_alternatives.reason: 31 extension files with heterogeneous callback signatures and per-extension ownership; every unsafe op and caller contract cannot be enumerated in one auditable package with the available evidence. The p25-x509 receipt still records 64 BLOCKED boundaries.
Spans provider key management, legacy digest init, SLH-DSA (32 sites) and multiple distinct ownership interiors. Largest volume and not a single reusable caller contract.

Smallest by count but not one mechanism (namemap vs thread). Establishing it requires concurrency evidence (Miri/Loom/TSan) that is NOT_RUN for those units; count alone is explicitly not the criterion.
The mechanism is CONTRACTED with 73 unaudited SSL BIO call sites; the two closure sites cannot support a mechanism-scope discharge.
Heterogeneous sub-mechanisms (DRBG vs CMS vs store; session ciph/conf/rsa) that each need per-site ownership analysis. Deferred, not rejected on principle.

caller_contract_shared.invocation_path: ENGINE_register_* or ENGINE_set_default_* -> engine_table_register (src/engine/eng_table.rs:273-296) -> engine_cleanup_add_first(cleanup) only when the table slot was NULL -> CLEANUP_STACK -> [withheld engine_cleanup_int] -> engine_cleanup_cb_free(item) -> cb() (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:684-694).
caller_contract_shared.registration_cardinality: At most one cleanup item per table slot lifetime: `engine_cleanup_add_first` runs only when `table.load().is_null()` (the `added` arm), and the slot is only returned to NULL by the cleanup that is currently unreachable. A second register/set_default on the same slot does not enqueue again.
caller_preconditions: Zero arguments: no caller-supplied pointer, extent, alignment or initialisation state.
The cleanup item stores the module's own function item (`Some(engine_unregister_all_*)`); no other writer targets CLEANUP_STACK with these nine (CALLER_SET/STATIC_PAIRING controls PASS).
The engine lock is initialised and not held by this thread at invocation (authority eng_lib.c:169-184: callbacks run before CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free; the callback takes the write lock itself).
No re-entrant engine API is active on this thread (B20 external contract: engine init/finish/destroy hooks must not re-enter; recursive write acquisition is refused).
implementation_may_assume: The slot is the module's own process-global `&'static EngineTableSlot`.
The lhash and EnginePile nodes are owned by the slot and released exactly once by `engine_table_cleanup` under the write lock.
A second invocation observes NULL and is a no-op.
caller_contract_shared.not_assumed: No caller-provided table, key, pointer or length. There is no wrong-arity, wrong-extent or uninitialised-argument obligation on this class.

caller_contract.who_may_call: Only `engine_cleanup_cb_free` (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:684-694), as the `sk_*_pop_free` callback of `engine_cleanup_int` (`engine_cleanup_cb_free(item)` -> `cb()`). `engine_cleanup_int` is withheld (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:696-700), so no invocation executes at this identity. `engine_cleanup_add_first` is the only writer that enqueues this pointer, and only `engine_table_register` reaches it (src/engine/eng_table.rs:294-296).
preconditions_the_caller_must_establish: The pointer stored in the cleanup item is exactly this module's function item (guaranteed by `Some(cb)` at the two registration sites and by no other writer; CALLER_SET/STATIC_PAIRING controls PASS).
Zero arguments: there is no pointer, extent, alignment or initialisation state supplied by the caller.

The engine read/write lock is initialised and is not held by this thread when `cb()` runs (authority crypto/engine/eng_lib.c:169-184 runs the callbacks before `CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free`; `engine_table_cleanup` takes the write lock itself).
No re-entrant engine API is active on this thread; B20 records the external contract that engine init/finish/destroy hooks must not re-enter (the crate refuses recursive write acquisition).
what_the_implementation_may_assume: The slot is this module's own process-global `&'static EngineTableSlot`; no caller can substitute another table.
The lhash in the slot and its EnginePile nodes are owned by the slot and released exactly once by `engine_table_cleanup` under the write lock.
A repeated invocation observes the swapped-out NULL slot and performs no release (idempotent by construction).

dispositions.ownership_lifetime: Slot: process-global static owned by the module. Table lhash and EnginePile nodes: owned by the slot, released by `engine_table_cleanup` under the engine write lock (`OPENSSL_LH_doall` + `OPENSSL_LH_free`). Cleanup item: owned by CLEANUP_STACK until `engine_cleanup_cb_free` releases it. The callback borrows no caller data and returns no value.
dispositions.failure_semantics: No return value. If `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock` fails (including an uninitialised/NULL lock), `engine_table_cleanup` returns before `swap`, leaving the slot populated and the table unreleased (leak/no-op, not UB). If the lock is acquired, the slot is swapped to NULL before any release, so a second call is a no-op. No path performed by this callback can double-free or use-after-free.
dispositions.residual_obligation: Shared callee dependency only: `engine_table_cleanup` (B20-TBL-3) is CONTRACTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED, and its `# Safety` does not state the lock-initialised precondition that the failing control exposes. The wrapper itself has no caller-supplied pointer obligation.

controls.name: engine::eng_table::tests::cleanup_nulls_the_slot_and_a_second_cleanup_is_a_no_op
controls.exact_output: panicked at src/engine/eng_table.rs:930: the first cleanup empties the slot; test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed (isolated); in the module filter: 8 passed; 1 failed
controls.root_cause: The test creates a slot and lhash directly but never calls `run_engine_lock_init`. `global_engine_lock()` is NULL, `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(NULL)` returns 0, and `engine_table_cleanup` returns before swapping the slot. The passing sibling `register_select_and_cleanup_round_trip_through_the_slot` calls `ENGINE_new`, which runs the lock init.
controls.classification: Test-isolation/functional defect; no UB observed. It exposes an unstated precondition of the shared callee (lock initialised), not a caller-supplied-pointer defect in the nine wrappers.
controls.fails_if: the callee stops swapping the slot before release, or the lock precondition is not established.

registry_change_proposal.state_json_change: NONE. Do not change `state.json#/mechanisms[id=C_ABI_CONTRACT].state`. A value of SAFETY_DISCHARGED is not scope-aware and would be consumed as a mechanism-wide claim.
registry_change_proposal.why_state_flip_is_inadmissible: `consumer_closure.py` loads mechanism states from state.json (build_receipt, ~12617-12630) and overlays CAMPAIGN-STATUS `mechanism_discharges` whose id prefix matches. In `adjudicate()` (12374-12399), a SAFETY_DISCHARGED mechanism is DISCHARGED only when the hard-coded `err_scope` (mechanism-discharge-ERR.json, mechanism ERR) covers the exact file/line. For C_ABI_CONTRACT the scope test cannot match, so every C_ABI_CONTRACT obligation would be set to UNKNOWN — a regression from BLOCKED, not a discharge. The 11 BLOCKED and 8 DISCHARGED C_ABI sites would all be re-opened as UNKNOWN.
registry_change_proposal.supported_path: Use the existing scoped-boundary path (`adjudicate()` step 2, 12402-12420): a site-enumerating receipt whose boundary `disposition` names the exact `src/file:line`, plus a CAMPAIGN-STATUS `scoped_boundary_discharges` entry listing those boundary ids. This is how `openssh-discharge` scoped 8 C_ABI sites without changing the mechanism state.

residuals.description: The shared callee `engine_table_cleanup` (B20-TBL-3, CONTRACTED) requires an initialised engine lock but its `# Safety` states only "the engine lock must not already be held". C3 exposes the omission: with a NULL lock it returns before swapping the slot. In production the lock is initialised by `ENGINE_new` before any registration, and registration is the only way to enqueue the callback, so the precondition is established transitively — but it is undocumented and not independently verified. This is a newly exposed obligation in the callee boundary, not in the nine wrappers.

C3 fails in isolation at adceec204 and on integrate/safe-c33 (identical test and callee). The full suite hides it because an earlier test initialises the lock. The idempotence/double-call property is therefore NOT established at this candidate.

B20-TBL-3 is CONTRACTED with residuals B20-R2 (table entries borrow ENGINE*, no reference) and B20-R3 (authority parity). The wrapper discharge would rest on a CONTRACTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED, dependency.

`engine_cleanup_int` is withheld (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:696-700), so the nine callbacks never run at this identity. The invocation-path assumptions are derived from the pinned authority, not exercised by the candidate.
No Miri/TSan/ASan for this scope. C4 is a functional serialisation test, not a race detector result.

newly_exposed: B20-TBL-3 / engine_table_cleanup: the engine lock must be initialised (non-NULL) before the call; the # Safety omits it and a targeted control fails when it is not.

The C3 failure is not claimed to be memory unsafety (UB); it is a no-op/leak and a contract-documentation defect.
No consumer SAFE_COMPATIBLE claim; no family graduation; no SEAL.

recommendation.detail: 0 of 9 obligations are recommended for DISCHARGED at adceec204. 9 of 9 caller contracts are CONTRACT_ESTABLISHED. The discharge is blocked by R1 (undocumented callee lock precondition), R2 (failing idempotence control), R3 (CONTRACTED dependency) and R4 (unreachable path).
repair_sequence: 1. Amend `engine_table_cleanup` # Safety (src/engine/eng_table.rs:512-517) to state the engine-lock-initialised precondition, or make the failure explicit and documented.
2. Repair `cleanup_nulls_the_slot_and_a_second_cleanup_is_a_no_op` to call `run_engine_lock_init` (as its sibling does) so it exercises the contract; re-run it in isolation and in the module filter.
3. Freeze the repaired source as S'; regenerate the closure; confirm the nine remain the same obligations and C3 passes.
4. Add the scoped-boundary receipt + CAMPAIGN-STATUS entry (proposal above); re-run the closure and confirm 9 BLOCKED -> 9 DISCHARGED and no other obligation changes state.
5. Independent BOUNDARY review (reviewer is not the author): re-run C1-C6 at S', challenge the caller set, table identity, reentrancy, and safe-API reachability.

reviewer_challenges: Caller-set completeness: verify no writer other than the two `Some(cb)` sites can enqueue these nine pointers, and that `engine_cleanup_add_first` is the only registration path (C2 only proves name occurrence, not pointer flow).

Table/pointer identity: verify each callback body's slot accessor and each registration's callback are the same module's pair, and that `EngineTableSlot` is a process-global static with no alternative writer.

Absence of reentrancy: verify the cleanup-stack walk does not hold the engine lock, and that an engine finish hook invoked under `engine_table_cleanup` cannot re-enter the engine API (B20 external contract; recursive write acquisition refused).
Safe-API reachability: confirm no safe Rust API invokes the nine outside `engine_cleanup_cb_free`, and that `engine_cleanup_int` remains withheld at the adjudicated candidate.

Callee dependency: decide whether a CONTRACTED B20-TBL-3 with B20-R2/R3 open can support a wrapper discharge, and whether the lock-init precondition is established by the registration path for every possible caller.
Control validity: independently reproduce C3's failure and confirm the root cause is the missing lock init, not a leaked lhash or a double free.
Identity: confirm the package's file hashes and closure hash match the candidate the reviewer runs; a source or tool change invalidates the package (§22).
